thread:
opsbot: ALERT: hosted-infer-usw2 p99 5xx SLO burn detected (15m window) :warning:
opsbot: metrics: p99_errors=1.8% (SLO 1%), total_requests=42k

sam: saw a pile of support tickets from a few customers in usw2 complaining about timeouts + 502/504s — linking here.

elaine: dashboard? logs?

sam: https://console.redwood/infer/dashboards/usw2-slo
sam: quick logs query I ran (CloudLogs):
```
resource=service/gateway severity>=ERROR | json.payload | where status_code >= 500 | summarize count() by upstream, status_code
```
sam: upstream shows a lot of 502 from auth-proxy and prefetcher v2 around 03:12-03:25 UTC

mike: hmm auth-proxy errors + timeouts -> could be token validation backend or KMS flakiness. Any deploys around then?

rachel: we had a quick rollback on billing-service at 03:10 to revert a rate-limit change. not sure if that's related but timeline overlaps.

sam: also seeing tracer gaps — many gateway->auth-proxy spans missing trace_id. sampling looks normal but traces stop at gateway.

elaine: can you paste a sample log line?

sam: example log: `level=error msg="upstream request failed" upstream=auth-proxy dur_ms=2001 status=502 err="upstream timeout" token_id=eyJ...`

mike: token_id present but auth-proxy not returning spans. suspect auth-proxy started dropping trace headers, maybe config change. Could also be connection churn to prefetch/kv-cache.

sam: repro command I used locally to simulate client behavior (expired token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <expired-token>" \n  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/models/gptx/outputs" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
sam: expired token gets 502 from gateway (should be 401) — gateway is timing out waiting for auth-proxy, not short-circuiting.

elaine: can we bump gateway timeout to fail fast while we triage? that will reduce customer pain.

mike: temporary patch: increase auth-proxy client retries to 1 and set connect timeout 500ms -> fail fast. I'll push a canary to usw2.

rachel: creating support note: customers X, Y, Z affected, initial ETA unknown. tagging CS.

oncall-bot: @sam assigned (oncall today) :pager:

sam: taking it. immediate next steps: 1) enable 100% trace sampling for gateway for 20m, 2) enable debug logs on auth-proxy, 3) push canary timeout change, 4) correlation queries for billing deploy hashes.

mike: doing canary now. rolling to 2 nodes in usw2. will post deploy id.

sam: trace sampling command: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/gateway TRACE_SAMPLING=1` (do for auth-proxy too). doing now.

mike: canary up (deploy id: canary-20260403-18). initial metrics look better on that subset — 5xx down for canary nodes.

elaine: while canary runs, run this correlation query to tie errors to billing deploy:
```
logs | where timestamp between("2026-04-03T03:00:00Z", "2026-04-03T03:30:00Z")
  | where upstream=="auth-proxy" and status>=500
  | summarize count() by deploy_hash, node
```
elaine: I ran it, and 85% of 5xx map to billing-deploy hash `b9f3c2` which was the rollback.

sam: ok so rollback may have introduced a config that makes billing service aggressively throttle token validation calls -> auth-proxy times out waiting -> gateway 502.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) revert the rollback (put previous config back on billing) OR 2) reduce billing service concurrency for token ops. Which do we prefer?

rachel: CS needs a tentative ETA for customers. which mitigation is quicker?

mike: revert rollback is fastest. I'll coordinate with billing on-call.

sam: meanwhile I'll flip gateway to fail fast on auth-proxy (lower timeout) to return 5xx -> 401 mapping in gateway so clients see auth errors instead of long timeouts. This reduces SLO impact.

mike: billing on-call @mike-billing notified, they're rolling a config revert now.

opsbot: note: increased tracing enabled for 20m

sam: after revert we should run a replay of affected requests against staging to confirm behavior. suggested script:
```
python tools/replay_requests.py --from=2026-04-03T03:05Z --to=2026-04-03T03:20Z --region=usw2 --auth=token
```

elaine: also add an alert to watch for trace drop ratio: `tracing.missing_spans_rate > 0.02 for 5m` — we got burned by that.

rachel: CS: told customers tentative fix being rolled, will update in 30m.

mike: billing revert complete (deploy id: billing-revert-b9f3c2). monitoring…

sam: metrics look normalizing on non-canary nodes. p99 errors dropping back under 0.8%. :thumbsup:

elaine: keep tracing sampling for another 10m then back to normal. capture a few sample traces to investigate missing-span root cause.

sam: follow-ups: - create postmortem if SLO hit persists - add unit test for token validation backpressure - add dashboards that map deploy hashes to 5xx spikes

rachel: leaving a note in support tickets and closing interim incident once p99 stable.

mike: thumbs. thanks all.

opsbot: ALERT RESOLVED: hosted-infer-usw2 p99 5xx SLO burn cleared at 03:48 UTC
